factories.name: newSearchStep
factories.description: Search one bounded page of the pages and data sources shared with the connection by title, continuing with Notion's cursor.

inputSchema.description: SearchInput selects one page of title matches among the pages and data sources shared with the connection.

objectType.description: ObjectType limits the results to pages or data sources; blank returns both.

pageSize.description: PageSize is the number of results to request, 1 to 100; zero requests 20.

query.description: Query is matched against titles; blank lists every shared page and data source.

sortDirection.description: SortDirection orders by last edit time; blank keeps Notion's relevance order.

startCursor.description: StartCursor continues a previous search with the same input; blank reads the first page.

factories.name: newQueryDatabaseStep
factories.description: Query one bounded page of a database's rows through its data source with a typed filter and sorts, continuing with Notion's cursor.

QueryFilter.description: QueryFilter is a typed Notion data source filter. Set exactly one of Property, Timestamp, And, and Or. A property condition names the property, its Type, a Condition the type supports, and the one value field the condition takes: Text for title, rich_text, url, email, phone_number, select, status, and multi_select; Number for number and unique_id; Checkbox for checkbox; Date for date; and ID for people and relation. FilterIsEmpty, FilterIsNotEmpty, and the relative date conditions such as FilterPastWeek take no value. A timestamp condition sets Timestamp, a date Condition, and Date. And and Or combine up to two levels of nested filters. An unsupported combination selects defect before any request is sent.

and.description: And matches pages that match every filter.

date.description: Date is a YYYY-MM-DD date or RFC 3339 date-time value.

id.description: ID is a Notion user ID for people or a page ID for relation.

or.description: Or matches pages that match any filter.

property.description: Property is the property name or ID that the condition reads.

text.description: Text is a text or option-name value.

timestamp.description: Timestamp filters on the page's creation or last edit time instead of a property.

type.description: Type is the property's Notion type, which selects the filter's shape.

QuerySort.description: QuerySort orders query results by a property or a timestamp. Set exactly one of Property and Timestamp.

direction.description: Direction is ascending or descending; blank is ascending.

property.description: Property is the property name or ID to sort by.

timestamp.description: Timestamp sorts by the page's creation or last edit time.

inputSchema.description: QueryDatabaseInput selects one page of a database's rows. Set exactly one of DataSourceID and DatabaseID.

dataSourceId.description: DataSourceID is the data source to query. In Notion, open the database's settings menu > Manage data sources and choose Copy data source ID.

databaseId.description: DatabaseID is the database ID from its URL, or the URL itself; the database must hold exactly one data source.

filter.description: Filter optionally limits the rows; nil returns every row.

pageSize.description: PageSize is the number of rows to request, 1 to 100; zero requests 50.

properties.description: Properties optionally lists the property names or IDs to return, at most 100; blank returns every property.

sorts.description: Sorts optionally orders the rows; Notion guarantees no order without one.

startCursor.description: StartCursor continues a previous query with the same input; blank reads the first page.

factories.name: newGetPageStep
factories.description: Read one page's properties and a bounded plain-text rendering of its top-level blocks.

maxBlocks.description: MaxBlocks bounds the top-level blocks read, 1 to 500; zero reads up to 100.

maxTextCharacters.description: MaxTextCharacters bounds Content.Text, 1 to 100,000 characters; zero keeps up to 20,000.

pageId.description: PageID is the page ID, with or without dashes, or the page's Notion URL.

skipContent.description: ShouldSkipContent reads only the page's properties, without its blocks.

factories.name: newCreatePageStep
factories.description: Create one database row with typed property values and optional plain-text body paragraphs. Sync durability persists the single-dispatch fence before sending so retries cannot duplicate an unconfirmed page.

DateRange.description: DateRange is a Notion date value: one date or date-time, or a range.

end.description: End optionally ends a range, in the same format as Start; blank means a single date.

start.description: Start is a YYYY-MM-DD date or an RFC 3339 date-time such as 2026-09-30T14:00:00Z.

timeZone.description: TimeZone optionally names an IANA time zone, such as America/Los_Angeles, for a date-time without an offset; blank uses the offset in Start.

PropertyValue.description: PropertyValue is one typed property value written to a Notion page. Type selects exactly one value field: Text for title and rich_text, Number, Checkbox, Option for select and status, Options for multi_select, Date, URL, Email, PhoneNumber, UserIDs for people, and PageIDs for relation. Setting a field that does not belong to Type selects defect. The zero value of the type's field clears the property, except that a checkbox needs an explicit value and a status needs an option name. Prefer the constructors such as TitleValue and SelectValue, and ClearedValue to clear a property on purpose. Writes replace the property's whole value: a multi_select, people, or relation value lists every entry the property keeps, so repeating the same write leaves the page unchanged.

email.description: Email is a plain email address.

number.description: Number is a finite number value.

option.description: Option is a select or status option name. Notion adds a missing select option to the data source; a status option must already exist.

options.description: Options lists multi_select option names, at most 100, without commas.

pageIds.description: PageIDs lists related page IDs for a relation value, at most 100.

phoneNumber.description: PhoneNumber is free-form phone text, such as +1 206 555 0100.

text.description: Text is the plain text of a title or rich_text value, at most 20,000 characters.

type.description: Type is the property's Notion type.

url.description: URL is an absolute URL value.

userIds.description: UserIDs lists Notion user IDs for a people value, at most 100.

inputSchema.description: CreatePageInput describes one database row. Set exactly one of DataSourceID and DatabaseID.

bodyText.description: BodyText is optional plain text for the page body, at most 50,000 characters in at most 100 paragraphs. Blank lines separate paragraphs, other line breaks stay inside a paragraph, and the text is never read as markup.

dataSourceId.description: DataSourceID is the data source that receives the row. In Notion, open the database's settings menu > Manage data sources and choose Copy data source ID.

databaseId.description: DatabaseID is the database ID from its URL, or the URL itself; the database must hold exactly one data source.

properties.description: Properties maps property names or IDs to typed values, at most 100. A property left out keeps the data source's default, such as an empty title.

factories.name: newUpdatePagePropertiesStep
factories.description: Set typed property values on one page with absolute values, so a repeated or duplicated update leaves the page unchanged.

DateRange.description: DateRange is a Notion date value: one date or date-time, or a range.

end.description: End optionally ends a range, in the same format as Start; blank means a single date.

start.description: Start is a YYYY-MM-DD date or an RFC 3339 date-time such as 2026-09-30T14:00:00Z.

timeZone.description: TimeZone optionally names an IANA time zone, such as America/Los_Angeles, for a date-time without an offset; blank uses the offset in Start.

PropertyValue.description: PropertyValue is one typed property value written to a Notion page. Type selects exactly one value field: Text for title and rich_text, Number, Checkbox, Option for select and status, Options for multi_select, Date, URL, Email, PhoneNumber, UserIDs for people, and PageIDs for relation. Setting a field that does not belong to Type selects defect. The zero value of the type's field clears the property, except that a checkbox needs an explicit value and a status needs an option name. Prefer the constructors such as TitleValue and SelectValue, and ClearedValue to clear a property on purpose. Writes replace the property's whole value: a multi_select, people, or relation value lists every entry the property keeps, so repeating the same write leaves the page unchanged.

email.description: Email is a plain email address.

number.description: Number is a finite number value.

option.description: Option is a select or status option name. Notion adds a missing select option to the data source; a status option must already exist.

options.description: Options lists multi_select option names, at most 100, without commas.

pageIds.description: PageIDs lists related page IDs for a relation value, at most 100.

phoneNumber.description: PhoneNumber is free-form phone text, such as +1 206 555 0100.

text.description: Text is the plain text of a title or rich_text value, at most 20,000 characters.

type.description: Type is the property's Notion type.

url.description: URL is an absolute URL value.

userIds.description: UserIDs lists Notion user IDs for a people value, at most 100.

inputSchema.description: UpdatePagePropertiesInput sets property values on one page. Properties left out keep their values; every listed value replaces the property's whole value, so repeating the same input leaves the page unchanged.

pageId.description: PageID is the page ID, with or without dashes, or the page's Notion URL.

properties.description: Properties maps property names or IDs to typed values, 1 to 100. Use ClearedValue to empty a property.
